tag: Episode 50 · A Name to Read, a Destiny to Write
title: A Name to Read, a Destiny to Write

beats.t: The phone rang twice. Instead of a third ring came a click. Every leaf of the World Tree rustled at once, then stopped.
Thank you for waiting. Destiny Customer Support. This is the universe.
The voice came from everywhere: tree, earth, Yeoni's phone. Excessively polite.
You know how long I waited? The queue was infinite!
Yes, valued customer. We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. We are currently experiencing high inquiry volumes across the universe.
The universe was the agent? The agent was the universe?
Both, apparently.
We've reviewed your case. Destiny-code damage: eighty-seven percent. Cause: Black Moon. Resolution: Black Moon eliminated. Four Pillars restored to eight of eight.
You knew everything?
Everything is recorded, valued customer. Processing was merely delayed.
Late is always the problem.
Neo grumbled under his breath. Yeoni almost laughed. At this particular moment, he had the least right to say that.
May I ask something? Does that record include everything I did?
Yes, valued customer. Without exception. The applause you erased and the name you returned are on the same page.
Seo Hanbi lowered her head without making excuses. Only her fingers tightened on the umbrella handle.
Then the money I earned from compatibility readings must be there too.
Yes. Three refund requests have been filed.
People complain to the universe? Who filed them?
One final procedure remains: completing Card Twenty-Three. An empty destiny invites something else in.
The blank card descended before Yeoni, along with a pen. The very ballpoint clipped to their notebook.
I write it? Write what? What if I misspell something?
One line. The line you write becomes this door's rule. Please choose carefully.
Yeoni. One line can be anything. Truly anything.
Yeoni took the pen. Too many wishes crowded their mind: their mother's year, Yundal's name, Seo Hanbi's first spring. And Neo.
For your information, upon completing their mission, guardians return to their original place, leaving their memories of this world behind. This is policy.
The hand holding the pen stopped. Yeoni looked at Neo. He didn't look surprised.
You knew?
From the beginning. When I return, I'm Park-whatever. Someone who doesn't know you.
Stop saying Park-whatever. It's irritating.
Their surroundings became the card corridor. Countless cards floated like stars, like the sky viewed from the World Tree's crown. It was quiet, as though only the two remained.
Then I can write that line. Neo returns with his memories. Like that.
You could.
But if I do...
Yeoni couldn't finish. They looked up. Paper leaves fallen from the World Tree still scattered the ground, their names erased.
I can't return those people's names. Dodam's. Museong's. Yundal's real name.
I know.
Why do you always know everything? So irritating.
Neo rested his forehead against Yeoni's shoulder. Warm breath touched them. The ends of his silver hair tickled their cheek.
You've already given me a name. That's enough. Write what you want.
That's the most unfair thing to say.
I know.
Yeoni buried their face in his shoulder. He smelled of rain mixed with sunlight. A scent that had been beside them before his appearance changed.
If I find you again, don't pretend you don't know me.
I won't be pretending. I truly won't know.
Then I'll make you know me. Even if I have to bombard you with bad ratings.
A little frightening.
Yeoni wiped their tears with the back of their hand and set the pen to the card. The writing was crooked. They didn't correct it.
[ 23 · THE DOOR · Every swallowed name returns to its owner. The door opens from inside too. ]
As the final word was written, the card shone. An illustration formed: one door. A half-open wooden door, with an umbrella leaning beside it.
Received. A fine line, valued customer. Especially the latter part.
I just wrote that part. It's only fair for a door to open from inside too.
Indeed. We had overlooked that clause. This door will now open from both sides.
Neo lifted his head, then pressed his lips together, as though he had caught the hidden meaning first.
The World Tree's leaves rose together. Writing refilled every erased paper. Names scattered on the wind, seeking their owners.
A drum sounded far away. Small hands playing a clumsy rhythm. Yeoni knew it, a rhythm heard on the Island of Expression.
Dodam. Dodam must have found their name.
Then singing. Not a crow's broken voice, but a boy's voice, clear and slightly trembling.
Museong. He's singing. No one's laughing at him. Though he's a little off-key.
Yundal looked at his palm. A name rode the wind and settled on its lines. He stared at it for a long time.
Ah.
What does it say?
Secret, remember? I said I'd tell you at my front door.
We're at a door! There's a door right there!
Yundal looked at the half-open wooden door and smiled as though conceding.
Saebyeok. Kang Saebyeok. Mom named me Dawn because I was born at five twenty in the morning.
Saebyeok. Much better than Yundal.
I'll still use Yundal for compatibility readings. Better for business.
Seo Hanbi lifted the inside of her cloak. The place where names had been sewn was empty. Only a few loose threads remained.
All gone. No names left for me to carry.
Do you miss them?
No. I feel light. It's been so long since I felt this light that it's a little strange.
Farewells began before the door. Nobody wanted to speak first. Finally, Moka folded his arms and stepped forward.
I'm staying here. Have to teach the island to sing again. Rap included.
Perhaps leave out the rap.
Rap is the point! Change that rating. Five stars this time.
Five stars. Because the flavor is a crime.
Don't delete the app. I'll message you. Seriously.
Yundal—no, Kang Saebyeok—offered his hand. Yeoni took it. A hand without a glove. Warm.
If we meet in reality, don't pretend you don't know me. I'm tired of being forgotten.
I'll pretend if you ask my birthday.
Occupational hazard. Incurable.
You've held that hand too long.
We're saying goodbye. Allow that much, Mr. Cat.
I gave you three seconds. They're up.
Seo Hanbi stood beside Yeoni, holding the umbrella with three layers of tape. She too would return through the same door. As names returned to their owners, the name Seo Hanbi returned to reality.
I have work to do over there. Much to repay. Without a ledger.
Finally, Neo remained. Sitting side by side before the door, the two gazed at it silently for a while.
Before the open door, the twenty-third card split into two lights. One showed a cherry-blossom riverbank, the other a moonlit World Tree.
The card you wrote does not command only a return. You may now choose where to make your life.
Whichever we choose, our memories remain? No condition that makes us lose someone again?
Memories and bonds are preserved through both doors. One is not a wrong answer, nor is the other an escape.
I'll follow your choice. If a guardian chooses even your ending for you, that isn't protection.
I'll return to reality and repair what I damaged. But your home is yours to choose, Yeoni.
Wherever you live, I'm sending you my rap. They say the twenty-third door doesn't block news.
Yeoni looked slowly at both doors. This time, it wasn't about surviving a structure someone else had arranged. It was choosing their own next spring.
[ The Twenty-Third Card · I choose the world I will live in ]
